snapshot.title: TNPSC History: Modern India (TN Focus)
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC GS Hook: Francis Day: Chennai. Rajaji: Vedaranyam. Vallalar: Sanmargam. 1801: Presidency. 1937: Rajaji.

quick_notes.title: British Entry
quick_notes.detail: Fort St. George (1639 - Francis Day). Madras Presidency formed in 1801.
quick_notes.explanation: The British first established a permanent settlement in India when they built Fort St. George in 1639. Fort St. George was a fortified trading post, and it was built by a British official named Francis Day. Later, in 1801, the British formed the Madras Presidency, which was a large administrative region that covered much of southern India and was ruled directly by the British East India Company.

quick_notes.title: Social Reforms
quick_notes.detail: St. Ramalinga Adigal (Vallalar - Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam). Ayya Vaikundar (Ayyavazhi).
quick_notes.explanation: St. Ramalinga Adigal, also known as Vallalar, founded the Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam, which means the Society for the Pure Path of Universal Harmony, to promote equality among all people and reject caste discrimination. Ayya Vaikundar started the Ayyavazhi belief system, which taught that all humans are equal and that worshipping one God without caste barriers is the true path. Both reformers lived in the 19th century in the Tamil region and focused on breaking down social hierarchies, especially the caste system, by encouraging people to worship together and treat everyone with respect. Their teachings emphasized simple, devotional practices and rejected rituals that separated people based on birth or wealth.

quick_notes.title: Leaders (Recap)
quick_notes.detail: Rajaji (Chakravarthi Rajagopalachari - "Mango of Salem"). K. Kamaraj (Kingmaker). Sathyamurti.
quick_notes.explanation: Chakravarthi Rajagopalachari, often called Rajaji, was a leader from Salem who was known as the "Mango of Salem" because of his sharp, sweet, and sometimes sour personality. K. Kamaraj was a powerful political strategist who helped make others the Prime Minister of India, earning him the title "Kingmaker." Sathyamurti was a prominent freedom fighter and a key leader in the Indian National Congress who mentored Kamaraj and fought for India's independence from British rule.

quick_notes.title: Civil Disobedience
quick_notes.detail: Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha (1930) - Led by Rajaji. From Trichy to Vedaranyam.
quick_notes.explanation: Civil Disobedience is a method of peaceful protest where people deliberately break a law they consider unfair, accepting the punishment to show their opposition. In 1930, as part of the larger Civil Disobedience Movement against British rule in India, C. Rajagopalachari, popularly known as Rajaji, led the Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha. This was a march from Trichy, which is the city of Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu, to V

quick_notes.title: 1937 Elections
quick_notes.detail: Congress won. Rajaji became Premier. Introduced Prohibition and Temple Entry authorization.
quick_notes.explanation: The 1937 Elections were elections held in British India for provincial legislative assemblies under the Government of India Act 1935. The Indian National Congress, a major political party working for independence, won a majority of seats in several provinces, including the Madras Presidency. In Madras, Congress leader Chakravarti Rajagopalachari, commonly called Rajaji, became the Premier (the head of the provincial government, similar to a Chief Minister today). His government introduced two major laws: Prohibition, which banned the sale and consumption of alcohol, and the Temple Entry Authorization Act, a law that allowed people from lower castes, who were previously forbidden, to enter Hindu temples. This was a significant step for social reform and the uplift of marginalized communities.
